thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: euc2 edge-proxy HTTP 5xx spike detected (past 5m). Auto-page to oncall. Rule: edge-proxy-euc2-5xx-threshold.

ada (oncall): I'm looking. Saw a sudden jump ~1841234400. Checking ALB/NLB and envoy metrics.

ada (oncall): Cloud console shows NLB target health flapping in AZ-b. Some targets in target-group tg-edge-euc2-b are UNHEALTHY.

javier (eng-sre): @ada can you paste the target health output? I can check route table / TG registration sync.

ada (oncall): pastebin of health: ```
TargetId: i-0d12345  Health: UNHEALTHY (Connection Refused)
TargetId: i-0d23456  Health: UNHEALTHY (503)
TargetId: i-0d34567  Health: healthy
```

sasha (eng-infra): I'm seeing a recent control-plane error when we pushed a security policy ~30m ago. There was a partial API failure in euc2 AZ-b that looks like it delayed NLB target updates.

kate (support): Customer alerts: several EU accounts reporting 502s on webhooks and embeddings ingestion. CS triage says ~40 customers reported between 1841234300-1841234600. Noted high error-rate for small subset of routes.

ada (oncall): Impact estimate: ~3-6% of requests in euc2, spike in 502/504 and some connection resets. No data loss reported yet. We'll add incident severity P1 for availability.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1841234567 (P1) — incident channel: #inc-1841234567. Pager duty: notified primary.

javier (eng-sre): Hypothesis: NLB target registration race where control-plane propagation lag caused some envoy frontends to send traffic to targets that were still being drained or failed health checks -> connection resets and 502s. Also seeing increased RSTs in envoy metrics for AZ-b.

ada (oncall): Quick mitigation: fail traffic away from AZ-b by updating ALB/NLB target routing weights and enabling cross-zone load balancing forcing healthy AZs to take traffic. Executing now.

sasha (eng-infra): To reduce blast radius, I'm disabling new deployments to euc2 and pausing autoscaler for edge instance group in AZ-b. Also re-registering healthy targets into tg-edge-euc2-b.

ada (oncall): Commands I ran: ```bash
# move traffic off AZ-b
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:tg:edge-euc2 --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
# re-register healthy instances
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:edge-euc2-b --targets Id=i-0d34567 Id=i-0d45678
```

javier (eng-sre): I'm rolling a quick envoy restart on the unhealthy frontends in AZ-b to clear stale connections. Doing a canary (2 nodes) first.

kate (support): Notifying top 10 affected customers with rollback guidance. Also added a note to status.redwood.ai: "Partial availability issues in EU-C2 region, engineers investigating" :writing_hand:.

monitoring-bot: Alert suppression engaged for related 5xx alerts in euc2 to reduce noise.

ada (oncall): Early indicators: after traffic shift and re-register, 5xx rate dropped from 4.9% -> 1.1% in ~4 minutes. RSTs decreased. Still above baseline.

javier (eng-sre): Looking at control-plane logs: saw `RouteUpdateTimeout` errors from the cloud provider's API in AZ-b between 1841234100-1841234350. That aligns with the initial burst. Propagation lag seems to have caused transient target mapping inconsistencies.

sasha (eng-infra): I've opened ticket with cloud provider referencing internal trace id cp-87654, asking for RCA on API propagation delays. We've started a manual reconciliation loop to ensure target group membership is synced.

ada (oncall): Next steps: 1) keep traffic routed away from AZ-b for 30m 2) finish full reconciliation of NLB target groups 3) roll healthy envoys in AZ-b 4) monitor for customer errors.

kate (support): Support notes: customers on EU-C2 who saw failures are being offered retry guidance and we've enabled a temporary retry policy at the ingress layer for non-idempotent webhook endpoints where safe.

ops-rotation: I'm taking the overnight handoff at 1841234800. Ada, leave a 1-line summary and what to watch on handoff.

ada (oncall): Handoff summary: P1 INC-1841234567 — euc2 AZ-b control-plane propagation lag caused NLB target desync -> increased 5xx and connection resets. Mitigations: traffic shifted off AZ-b, re-registered healthy targets, canary envoy restarts, deployments paused. Monitor 5xx rate (edge-proxy.5xx.rate) and RSTs (envoy.tcp.rst). Keep cloud provider ticket open.

ada (oncall): Things to watch: if 5xx >2% for >10m, re-escalate to eng-sre and consider full AZ failover. Check status.redwood.ai for customer messaging updates.

javier (eng-sre): I'll stay on pager standby in case the reconcilers show re-registrations flipping back.

sasha (eng-infra): Note for postmortem: examine our reliance on immediate control-plane confirmations for TG updates and consider adding idempotent reconciliation and delayed fail-open logic to avoid partial mapping during API hiccups.

kate (support): I'll coordinate follow-ups and add affected customer list to the incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1841234567 moved to monitoring state. Assigned to ada (oncall).

ops-rotation: Thanks, picking up now. Good job triaging everyone. :thumbsup:

ada (oncall): handing off, logging final note before signoff. Keep paging if it flares back up.

javier (eng-sre): Logged a short runbook step: `reconcile-nlb-targets --region euc2 --az b` in inc page.

sasha (eng-infra): leaving a link to cloud provider ticket: https://cloudprovider.example.com/cases/CP-87654 (internal)

kate (support): final note: Support paged top 10 customers and will follow up within 2 hours.

monitoring-bot: Metrics stabilized. 5xx rate back to 0.4% (baseline 0.3%). Closing noisy alerts.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1841234567 status: RESOLVED -> monitoring-> stable. Postmortem required (P1). Assign to eng-infra + eng-sre.

ada (oncall): closing thread here. Will open a postmortem ticket and link to this thread.
